finding.claim: SQL injection in /admin/drop: the user-supplied form value 't' is concatenated directly into a DROP TABLE statement.
finding.source: r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27 (query string or POST body, fully attacker-controlled)
finding.sink: runSQL("DROP TABLE " + ...) at api.go:27 (runSQL defined at api.go:41, stub here; assumed to execute against the DB)

trace.note: /admin/drop is registered on DefaultServeMux with no auth or method middleware in this file
user pulled from request context; unchecked type assertion
raw FormValue('t') concatenated into SQL and passed to runSQL

finding.guards_checked: No validation, allowlist, identifier quoting or parameterization on 't'. The only guard (Authorize) does not stop execution, so it does not gate this sink in practice.

verdict.guard_found: none effective. Authorize at api.go:26 is called as a bare statement and its error is discarded, so it does not gate the sink. There is no allowlist, identifier quoting, or parameterization on the value at api.go:27. The unchecked type assertion at api.go:25 panics when the context has no *User, which stops the request before the sink, but it is not an authorization control. No middleware in the provided code sets the "user" context value, and no auth wraps the route registered at api.go:44.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches (api.go:24-27, 44), and the unused Authorize result at api.go:26 means any user who reaches the handler with a *User in context can run the injected statement at api.go:27. Whether that happens depends on an auth middleware that sets the "user" context value (api.go:22, api.go:25), which is not in the provided code, and without it the handler panics before reaching the sink, so the finding cannot be confirmed from this code alone.

finding.claim: Authorization bypass on /admin/drop: the result of Authorize(u, "dba") is ignored, so any caller who reaches the handler can run the destructive operation regardless of roles.
finding.source: Any request reaching the handler, including a user with Roles=[] or an unrelated role, via the context user set at api.go:25
finding.sink: Protected operation runSQL("DROP TABLE ...") at api.go:27

trace.note: Authorize returns errors.New("forbidden") when the role is absent
Authorize's error is dropped; no early return

finding.guards_checked: Authorize (api.go:13-20) is correct in isolation. The bug is only in the caller at api.go:26, which lacks the 'if err := ...; err != nil { return }' check used correctly in vacuum (api.go:33-36).

verdict.guard_found: Authorize (api.go:13-20) is the only role check. Its error return is discarded by the bare call at api.go:26, so no control blocks the path. The correct pattern at api.go:33-36 is not used in dropTable.
verdict.reason: At api.go:26 the result of Authorize(u, "dba") is a bare statement, so when it returns errors.New("forbidden") at api.go:19 execution continues to runSQL("DROP TABLE " + ...) at api.go:27 for any authenticated user whose context carries a *User. The trace matches the file. The only assumption is that the middleware setting the "user" context value (not in this directory) admits low-privilege users, which the handler is designed to exclude.

finding.claim: State-changing GET/CSRF exposure on /admin/drop: the handler accepts any HTTP method and reads form values from the query string, with no CSRF token or Origin check.
finding.source: Cross-site page or link causing the victim's browser to request /admin/drop?t=... (precondition: the admin's session is cookie-based, which is not visible in this repo)

trace.note: r.FormValue reads URL query params as well as POST body

finding.guards_checked: No method check (compare only the handler shape), no CSRF token, no SameSite or Origin validation in this file. Severity depends on the unseen auth layer. Attack is largely moot while F1/F2 allow any authenticated user to drop tables.

verdict.guard_found: None against CSRF. The only check on this path, Authorize at api.go:26, returns an error that is discarded as a bare statement, so it blocks nothing. No CSRF token, Origin, Referer, or method check exists in api.go. Route registration at api.go:44 has no method restriction, and r.FormValue at api.go:27 reads query parameters as well as the body.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (api.go:44 registers the route for every method, and api.go:27 takes the table name from FormValue, which includes the query string), and no CSRF guard exists in api.go. Whether a cross-site request carries the victim's credentials depends on the session mechanism, which is not in this repo, so exploitability cannot be decided here.

finding.claim: Authentication is assumed but not enforced here: userFrom performs an unchecked type assertion, and nothing in this codebase sets the "user" context value. Requests without it panic.
finding.sink: Type assertion r.Context().Value("user").(*User) at api.go:22, reached from api.go:25 and api.go:32

trace.note: admin routes registered with no auth wrapper
Value("user") returns nil when unset; .(*User) panics

finding.guards_checked: No authentication middleware in the repo. net/http recovers the panic per request, so the impact is a per-request crash/500 unless the missing auth layer is added elsewhere. The string context key "user" is also collision-prone. Lower severity; it matters if the auth middleware is absent in deployment.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only "user" lookup is the unchecked assertion at api.go:22, nothing in the repo sets the "user" context value (grep finds no WithValue), and /admin/drop and /admin/vacuum are registered with no auth wrapper at api.go:44-45. Authorize (api.go:13) is only reached after userFrom, so it never runs for an unauthenticated request.
verdict.reason: The trace holds: an anonymous request to /admin/drop (api.go:44) reaches userFrom at api.go:25, where Value("user") is nil and the non-comma-ok assertion at api.go:22 panics, and no control at api.go:13-45 stops it. The impact is narrower than "unauthenticated admin access": net/http recovers the panic per request, so the practical effect is a dropped connection or 500, not a process crash or executed SQL. A related issue the candidate missed is that dropTable discards Authorize's result at api.go:26, so any caller that does get a non-dba user (for example, via middleware outside this repo) still reaches runSQL at api.go:27.
